reasoning_ladder.represent: $\vec{a} = a_x \hat{i} + a_y \hat{j} = 0\,\hat{i} - g\,\hat{j}$ — Force resolution along Cartesian basis vectors.

reasoning_ladder.interpret: $\vec{v}(t) = u_x\,\hat{i} + (u_y - gt)\,\hat{j}$ — The two orthogonal motions evolve independently under a shared universal time clock.

questions.stem: A football is kicked into the air at an angle $\theta = 45.0^\circ$ above horizontal ground. At the apex (highest point) of its curved parabolic trajectory, what is the magnitude of its velocity vector, and why is it NOT zero?

options.A: Velocity magnitude is $u \cos 45.0^\circ = u / \sqrt{2} \neq 0$ because only vertical velocity momentarily vanishes ($v_y = 0$), while horizontal velocity $v_x = u_x$ persists unchanged.
options.B: Velocity magnitude is zero because at the top of any trajectory an object must momentarily come to rest.
options.C: Velocity magnitude is $u$ because energy is conserved and speed never changes.
options.D: Velocity magnitude is $u \sin 45.0^\circ$ directed vertically downward.

qrt_contract.protected_work_W: Explain non-zero apex velocity invariant through persistence of horizontal component.

A.diagnostic: Correct. At the apex of 2D projectile motion, $v_y = 0$ at the turning point of vertical motion. However, horizontal velocity $v_x = u \cos\theta$ is unaffected by gravity and remains non-zero. The speed is $v_{\text{apex}} = \sqrt{v_x^2 + 0^2} = u \cos\theta > 0$.

B.diagnostic: Confuses 2D oblique projectile motion with 1D purely vertical throw where apex speed is indeed zero.

C.diagnostic: Ignores gravitational potential energy at apex: kinetic energy is minimum, not constant.

D.diagnostic: Labels apex velocity as vertical instead of purely horizontal.

progressive_hints.prompt_question: What defines the highest point (apex) of a projectile trajectory in terms of vertical velocity?
progressive_hints.reveal_text: At the apex, the projectile stops ascending and begins descending; thus its vertical velocity momentarily vanishes: $v_y = 0$.

progressive_hints.title: Geometric Representation
progressive_hints.prompt_question: Does the horizontal velocity $v_x$ change anywhere during the flight in the absence of air resistance?
progressive_hints.reveal_text: No! Because $a_x = 0$, $v_x(t) = u \cos\theta$ remains constant at every single instant throughout the flight, including at the apex.

progressive_hints.title: First Mathematical Pivot
progressive_hints.prompt_question: What is the net speed $v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2}$ at the apex?

reasoning_ladder.understand: $\text{Trajectory turning point in 2D Euclidean coordinate space.}$ — Extreme value of vertical coordinate y(t).
reasoning_ladder.represent: $\vec{v} = v_x \hat{i} + v_y \hat{j},\quad v_x = u\cos\theta,\quad v_y = u\sin\theta - gt$ — Cartesian components of velocity.
reasoning_ladder.connect: $\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \iff v_y(t_{\text{apex}}) = 0$ — First derivative condition for maximum altitude.
reasoning_ladder.calculate: $|\vec{v}(t_{\text{apex}})| = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{(u\cos 45^\circ)^2 + 0^2} = u\cos 45^\circ = \frac{u}{\sqrt{2}} \neq 0$ — Pythagorean norm evaluation at apex.
reasoning_ladder.interpret: $\text{The ball continues traveling horizontally at } u/\sqrt{2} \text{ at the apex.}$ — Dispels the common learner trap of transferring 1D zero-speed intuition to 2D motion.

derivation_steps: Step 1 (Understand the physical regime): $\text{Trajectory turning point in 2D Euclidean coordinate space.}$ [Extreme value of vertical coordinate y(t).]
Step 2 (Represent the physical configuration): $\vec{v} = v_x \hat{i} + v_y \hat{j},\quad v_x = u\cos\theta,\quad v_y = u\sin\theta - gt$ [Cartesian components of velocity.]
Step 3 (Connect governing physical laws): $\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \iff v_y(t_{\text{apex}}) = 0$ [First derivative condition for maximum altitude.]

Step 4 (Calculate & execute formal derivation): $|\vec{v}(t_{\text{apex}})| = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{(u\cos 45^\circ)^2 + 0^2} = u\cos 45^\circ = \frac{u}{\sqrt{2}} \neq 0$ [Pythagorean norm evaluation at apex.]

Step 5 (Interpret the physical outcome): $\text{The ball continues traveling horizontally at } u/\sqrt{2} \text{ at the apex.}$ [Dispels the common learner trap of transferring 1D zero-speed intuition to 2D motion.]

questions.stem: A particle is launched from level ground with velocity components $u_x = 20.0\text{ m/s}$ and $u_y = 50.0\text{ m/s}$ ($g = 10.0\text{ m/s}^2$). At what two distinct instants of time $t_1$ and $t_2$ during its flight does its instantaneous velocity vector make an angle of $45.0^\circ$ with the horizontal?

qrt_contract.protected_work_W: Model dual-instant geometric angle condition and exploit temporal apex reflection symmetry.

A.diagnostic: Correct. Angle of $45^\circ$ with horizontal requires $|v_y| / v_x = \tan 45^\circ = 1 \implies v_y = \pm v_x = \pm 20.0\text{ m/s}$. Ascending: $50 - 10t = +20 \implies t_1 = 3.0\text{ s}$. Descending: $50 - 10t = -20 \implies t_2 = 7.0\text{ s}$.

B.diagnostic: Computes incorrect time intervals from arithmetic error in solving $50 - 10t = 20$.

C.diagnostic: Uses $v_y = 0$ for one of the times, confusing $45^\circ$ condition with apex.

D.diagnostic: Selects apex time ($t = 5\text{ s}$) as the second instant.

progressive_hints.title: Decisive Physical Invariant
progressive_hints.prompt_question: What mathematical condition ensures a velocity vector makes an angle of $45.0^\circ$ with the horizontal?
progressive_hints.reveal_text: An angle of $45^\circ$ means $\tan\theta = \frac{|v_y|}{v_x} = 1$, which requires $|v_y| = v_x$.

progressive_hints.title: Geometric Representation
progressive_hints.prompt_question: What are the two possible algebraic values for the vertical component $v_y$?
progressive_hints.reveal_text: Since $v_x = 20.0\text{ m/s}$ is constant, $v_y = +20.0\text{ m/s}$ (while ascending) and $v_y = -20.0\text{ m/s}$ (while descending).

progressive_hints.title: First Mathematical Pivot
progressive_hints.prompt_question: Substitute $v_y(t) = u_y - gt = 50.0 - 10.0t$ for both cases.
progressive_hints.reveal_text: Case 1: $50.0 - 10.0t = +20.0 \implies 10t = 30 \implies t_1 = 3.0\text{ s}$. Case 2: $50.0 - 10.0t = -20.0 \implies 10t = 70 \implies t_2 = 7.0\text{ s}$.

reasoning_ladder.understand: $\theta(t) = \pm 45^\circ \iff \frac{v_y(t)}{v_x} = \pm 1$ — Geometric constraint on velocity orientation.
reasoning_ladder.represent: $v_x = 20.0\text{ m/s},\quad v_y(t) = 50.0 - 10.0t$ — Cartesian kinematic velocity components.
reasoning_ladder.connect: $v_y(t) = \pm v_x = \pm 20.0\text{ m/s}$ — Definition of 45-degree angle in Quadrants I and IV.
reasoning_ladder.calculate: $50.0 - 10t_1 = 20.0 \implies t_1 = 3.0\text{ s};\quad 50.0 - 10t_2 = -20.0 \implies t_2 = 7.0\text{ s}$ — Linear algebraic solution of both branches.
reasoning_ladder.interpret: $t_{\text{apex}} = \frac{50}{10} = 5.0\text{ s};\quad t_1 = 5 - 2 = 3.0\text{ s},\quad t_2 = 5 + 2 = 7.0\text{ s}$ — Demonstrates perfect time reflection symmetry around the trajectory apex.

derivation_steps: Step 1 (Understand the physical regime): $\theta(t) = \pm 45^\circ \iff \frac{v_y(t)}{v_x} = \pm 1$ [Geometric constraint on velocity orientation.]
Step 2 (Represent the physical configuration): $v_x = 20.0\text{ m/s},\quad v_y(t) = 50.0 - 10.0t$ [Cartesian kinematic velocity components.]
Step 3 (Connect governing physical laws): $v_y(t) = \pm v_x = \pm 20.0\text{ m/s}$ [Definition of 45-degree angle in Quadrants I and IV.]
Step 4 (Calculate & execute formal derivation): $50.0 - 10t_1 = 20.0 \implies t_1 = 3.0\text{ s};\quad 50.0 - 10t_2 = -20.0 \implies t_2 = 7.0\text{ s}$ [Linear algebraic solution of both branches.]

Step 5 (Interpret the physical outcome): $t_{\text{apex}} = \frac{50}{10} = 5.0\text{ s};\quad t_1 = 5 - 2 = 3.0\text{ s},\quad t_2 = 5 + 2 = 7.0\text{ s}$ [Demonstrates perfect time reflection symmetry around the trajectory apex.]

questions.stem: An airplane has an airspeed (speed relative to the air) of $v_{\text{air}} = 200.0\text{ km/h}$. A steady wind blows from the North toward the South with speed $v_{\text{wind}} = 50.0\text{ km/h}$. If the navigator wishes to fly the aircraft on a ground track due East, at what crab angle $\theta$ North of East must the pilot point the airplane's nose, and what will be the resulting ground speed $v_{\text{ground}}$?

options.A: Heading: $\theta = \arcsin(0.25) \approx 14.48^\circ\text{ North of East};\quad v_{\text{ground}} = \sqrt{200.0^2 - 50.0^2} = 50\sqrt{15} \approx 193.65\text{ km/h}$
options.B: Heading: $\theta = 45.0^\circ\text{ North of East};\quad v_{\text{ground}} = 150.0\text{ km/h}$
options.C: Heading: $\theta = 14.48^\circ\text{ South of East};\quad v_{\text{ground}} = 206.16\text{ km/h}$

qrt_contract.protected_work_W: Synthesize 2D aircraft crab angle heading and evaluate effective ground velocity.

A.diagnostic: Correct. Wind blows South ($-y$). To maintain a track due East ($+x$), the airplane's northward velocity component must cancel the wind: $v_{\text{air}} \sin\theta = v_{\text{wind}} \implies \sin\theta = \frac{50.0}{200.0} = 0.25 \implies \theta = \arcsin(0.25) \approx 14.48^\circ$ North of East. Ground speed is the remaining eastward component: $v_{\text{ground}} = v_{\text{air}} \cos\theta = \sqrt{200^2 - 50^2} = \sqrt{40000 - 2500} = \sqrt{37500} = 50\sqrt{15} \approx 193.65\text{ km/h}$.

B.diagnostic: Subtracts speeds linearly ($200 - 50 = 150$) and guesses $45^\circ$.

C.diagnostic: Heads South into the wind drift, doubling the southward drift.

D.diagnostic: Ignores wind drift, heading due East and allowing aircraft to drift South.

A.diagnostic: Correct. Normal centripetal acceleration is $a_n = \frac{v^2}{\rho} = \frac{10.0^2}{20.0} = \frac{100.0}{20.0} = 5.0\text{ m/s}^2$.
